title: pvCleantoGrid
body:
## pvCleantoGrid

Merges coincident or nearly coincident points and converts any dataset to an unstructured grid, e.g. to join blocks that share faces or to feed an operation that needs unstructured input. Merging uses Tolerance (fraction of the bounding-box diagonal) or AbsoluteTolerance, and PointDataWeightingStrategy decides how data on merged points is combined. Use cleanGrid for the common case with Schemaxis defaults.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Converting large structured grids to unstructured grids can use much more memory.
- A tolerance that is too large fuses distinct points and collapses small cells.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `CleantoGrid`. Identity: `filters/CleanUnstructuredGrid`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Clean to Grid filter. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AbsoluteTolerance` | When merging nearby points and using absolute tolerance (see ToleranceIsAbsolute property), this property specifies the tolerance for performing merging in the spatial units of the input data set. | `{"minimum":0.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.0` |
| `PointDataWeightingStrategy` | Select how to merge data located on merged points: - Take First Point (default): the point with the lowest index imposes its data on to the merged point - Average by Number: a number average is performed on all the duplicate points - Average by Spatial Density: an average by attached cell volume (i.e. for every cell the point is connected to sum cell_volume/number_cell_points) is performed on the point data | `{"type":"enum","values":["Take First Point","Average by Number","Average by Spatial Density"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Take First Point"` |
| `RemovePointsWithoutCells` | When true, points that no cell uses are dropped from the output, together with their point data; when false they are kept as free points. Removing them gives a cleaner mesh for export, while keeping them preserves point counts and indices of point clouds. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `Tolerance` | When merging nearby points and not using absolute tolerance (see ToleranceIsAbsolute property), this property specifies the tolerance for performing merging as a fraction of the length of the diagonal of the bounding box of the input data set. | `{"maximum":1.0,"minimum":0.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.0` |
| `ToleranceIsAbsolute` | This property determines whether to use absolute or relative (a percentage of the bounding box) tolerance when performing point merging. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvCleantoGrid",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
